concepts.learning_objective: Describe the structure of the epidermis and the role of the cuticle in preventing water loss.
Describe the structure of stomata, guard cells and subsidiary cells that form the stomatal apparatus.
Distinguish unicellular root hairs from the usually multicellular trichomes of the shoot and state their roles.
Identify the tissues and regions that make up the ground tissue system, including mesophyll in leaves.
Classify vascular bundles as radial or conjoint and as open or closed on the basis of xylem-phloem arrangement and cambium.
Describe the tissue layers of a dicot root from the epiblema to the stele, including endodermis and pericycle.
Compare monocot and dicot roots in the number of xylem bundles, size of pith and secondary growth.
Describe the hypodermis, cortex, endodermis, pericycle, vascular bundles and pith of a young dicot stem.
Identify the features of a monocot stem and use them to tell it apart from a dicot stem.
Describe the epidermis, palisade and spongy mesophyll and vascular system of a dorsiventral (dicot) leaf.
State how an isobilateral (monocot) leaf differs from a dorsiventral leaf in stomata, mesophyll and vascular bundles.
Explain how bulliform cells in grass leaves help reduce water loss under water stress.
